description:
## PetWorld overview
Dashboard child `workspace.home` at `/app/home`, rendered in the confirmed workspace outlet; navigation, main landmark and shell remain parent-owned.

Uses verified `petData` and `countryData` app services by opaque ID, with no page-level HTTP. Inventory, available pets and countries load concurrently through independently caught Angular promises. Each resource has its own loading/error/empty/retry state; failed or pending metrics display an em dash, never a fabricated zero. Inventory counts are independent server reports, not list totals. Featured cards show at most three actual records explicitly marked available. Country and unique continent counts derive from the successful normalized country dataset.

Refresh bypasses service caches and is disabled while any page request runs. Initial loads may use service caches. A last successful full refresh timestamp is recorded only after all three forced requests succeed; partial failures do not advance it. Individual retries do not reset other sections.

Reuses app-owned pw-stat-card, pw-pet-card and pw-feedback. Built-in Grid tracks use responsive CSS custom-property values for exact 1/2/4 metrics, 1/3 pets and 1/2 editorial panels; Box/Grid metadata owns structure. Core Badge supplies decorative paw/globe icons; no images, invented store locations or adoption claims.

The parent is confirmed. Destination child files were not available at creation: content links select exact workspace.pets/workspace.countries states when registered, otherwise use the parent shell's agreed #!/app/pets and #!/app/countries paths. The reused pet card owns its workspace.pet-detail link contract; that child must be registered by the app. No duplicate navigation is created.
name: home

variables.body:
const state = $ctrl.resources.inventory;
return !state.loading && !state.error && state.value !== null && ['available', 'pending', 'sold'].every(key => !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(state.value, key));
